title: Shah Rukh Khan Is Spending ₹50 Crore on a Single Scene. King Is Coming for Christmas — and the Whole World Calendar.
excerpt: A 350-crore budget, Suhana Khan's big-screen debut, a Deepika reunion, and a Christmas showdown with Avengers and Dune. The King has decided he's ending the year on his own throne.
body:
The teaser opened with a roar. Salt-and-pepper hair, blood on the brow, a man crashing through a glass ceiling onto the floor of a high-rise and snarling "Darr nahi, dehshat hoon" — I am not fear, I am destruction. By the next morning, every NRI group chat from Edison to Hounslow had the same three words pinned at the top: **It's King Time**.

<youtube></youtube>

**Shah Rukh Khan** does not make small returns. After *Pathaan*, *Jawan* and *Dunki* turned 2023 into the most lucrative comeback in Hindi film history, the obvious question was never *if* he would come back, but *how big*. The answer has a number attached now, and it is staggering: **King**, his reunion with *Pathaan* and *War* director **Siddharth Anand**, is being mounted on a reported budget in the ₹350–400 crore range, making it one of the most expensive films India has ever produced.

> "#KING is Ready to ROAR on 24.12.2026 in Cinemas." — Shah Rukh Khan, on X

Here is the detail that tells you exactly what kind of spectacle this is. The team recently wrapped a ten-day action schedule in Europe — a single sequence — at a cost of **₹50 crore**. That is roughly ₹5 crore a day, and it puts one set-piece in *King* above the entire introductory-sequence budget of *RRR*. Anand, the man who shot *War* in the Arctic Circle and sent a frozen-lake chase through Siberia in *Pathaan*, has reportedly designed **six major action set-pieces** for this film, filmed on real international locations rather than green screens. Think less Bollywood backlot, more *Mission: Impossible*. He is done with studio fakery, and the bank statements prove it.

Then there is the cast, which reads like a Karan Johar dinner party that got out of hand. Alongside SRK, *King* marks the big-screen debut of his daughter **Suhana Khan**, stepping up from Zoya Akhtar's Netflix film *The Archies* into a full-blown action ensemble under her father's protective glare. **Deepika Padukone** returns to share the frame with Khan once more — their sixth outing together after *Om Shanti Om*, *Chennai Express*, *Happy New Year*, *Pathaan* and *Jawan*, a pairing that has never once failed at the box office. **Abhishek Bachchan** turns full villain as the main antagonist, **Rani Mukerji** is back in the SRK universe after years away, and the supporting roster — Anil Kapoor, Jaideep Ahlawat, Arshad Warsi, Saurabh Shukla, Abhay Verma, Raghav Juyal — is deep enough to headline three other movies.

The road here hasn't been entirely smooth. A desert sequence featuring Anil Kapoor and Suhana, originally slated for Dubai this spring, was quietly pulled amid regional tensions in the Middle East and rebuilt on a massive recreated set in Mumbai's Vile Parle. "They've gone all out to match the scale Siddharth envisioned," a source on the production said — a chase that explodes into close combat, now shot under fully controlled lighting. For a film this size, control is the whole point.

What makes *King* genuinely fascinating for the diaspora isn't just the scale — it's the calendar gamble. The makers have locked **December 24, 2026**, planting the SRK flag squarely on Christmas weekend. They deliberately kept a 45-day cushion from Nitesh Tiwari's *Ramayana* in mid-November, with a source noting that SRK and Anand "don't want to hurt the business of that divine saga." But Christmas is where it gets spicy. A week earlier, on December 18, Hollywood drops two of its heaviest hitters at once — **Avengers: Doomsday** and **Dune: Part Three** — both arriving in Indian multiplexes with global momentum.

In most years, two Marvel-and-Villeneuve titans landing days before your release would be a death sentence for screen counts. With Shah Rukh Khan, the math bends. His films command a loyalty in Indian and overseas markets that no franchise can manufacture, and *King* has reportedly already locked an India distribution deal worth around **₹250 crore** — a sign that exhibitors are betting he'll hold his screens against the Avengers and the sandworms alike.

For NRIs, the Christmas slot is almost too perfect. December 24 means the film lands right as families across the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf are home for the holidays, theatres packed, *King* playing on premium IMAX screens beside the Hollywood giants. *King* will release worldwide in cinemas — expect the now-familiar SRK rollout of advance US and UK shows from Red Chillies Entertainment.

Darr nahi, dehshat. The man is 60, spending ₹50 crore on a single scene, debuting his daughter, reuniting with Deepika, and daring Marvel to share his Christmas. If anyone has earned the throne for the holidays, it's him.
